newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil settles $1.00 a tonne higher.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil settles $1.00 a tonne higher.

text.p: IPE Nov gas oil settled $1.00 a tonne higher with NYMEX heating oil leading the way up across the barrel on forecasts of a cold snap in the U.S. northeast, dealers said.
Nov gas oil ended at $219.75 with dealers seeing scope for further increases ahead of the contract's expiry on Tuesday.
"The heating oil is being supported by forecasts of below normal temperatures in the Northeast, including a smattering of snow in New York city at the weekend," a futures broker said.
"For once, gas oil in London is taking a back seat to NYMEX heating oil," he added.
But the broker said the focus should be on gasoline with a combination of short-covering and news that BP America planned to shut its Lima, Ohio refinery helping to lift unleaded higher.
Dec gasoline traded up $1.00 a gallon at $64.80 a gallon on NYMEX at 1756 GMT.

IPE Brent was also lifted higher by stronger gas oil and some buying interest in the late afternoon session. Dec Brent rose to an intraday high of $22.72 a barrel before slipping back to $22.63, up 42 cents by 1758 GMT.
WTI went up to a new high and a few stops went off on the Brent," a floor broker said.

Forecasts of rising oil demand in the final quarter of this year by the International Energy Agency were shrugged off by the market. Brokers said production was also set to rise, helping to alleviate the acute stock shortages.
